title: Redwood discovery - Sierra AI - latency & throughput
summary: Intro discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency and token/sec benchmarking. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for low-jitter latency at scale. Agreed to run a short benchmark with Sierra sample prompts; Redwood to send pricing and security docs.
next_steps: Maya to send hosted vs dedicated pricing and short product brief (by 2026-05-01)
Ravi to share benchmark plan and provision dedicated test cluster if needed (by 2026-05-04)
Sierra (Ethan) to upload sample prompts and target p95s to shared drive (by 2026-05-01)
Schedule technical deep dive / benchmarking kickoff (Ravi + Ethan) week of 2026-05-04
action_items: Maya Chen: Email pricing + one-pager comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private - due 2026-05-01
Ravi Patel: Draft benchmark test plan (concurrency, token lengths, streaming vs non-streaming) and provisioning steps - due 2026-05-04
Ethan Wu: Share canonical prompt set (50-100 examples) & current infra perf numbers - due 2026-05-01
Priya Desai: List security requirements (KMS, SAML, data residency) - due 2026-05-03
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting started. Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
[00:05] Lara Gomez: hi i'm lara, cto at sierra ai, we run a real-time inference platform for recommendations and conversational shopping. ethan and priy a on the call too.
[00:12] Ethan Wu: hi all, lead ml eng. we're evaluating Redwood for inference - primarily worried about p95 jitter at scale.
[00:20] Maya Chen: great, quick background - i'm maya, account exec; ravi is our solutions engineer, he'll cover latency/bench details.
[00:26] Ravi Patel: hi, yeah, we'll dig into p95 targets and how dedicated vs hosted behave under concurrency and streaming.
[00:32] Noah Kim: hi i'm noah infra - want to understand network/topology for VPC peering.
[00:37] Priya Desai: and security - SOC2, KMS, SSO requirements.
[00:40] Maya Chen: perfect. can you share current targets and load shape? p95 target, typical token lengths, concurrency?
[00:47] Ethan Wu: our ideal p95 for short responses (~32 tokens) is sub 250 ms; for mid-sized generative responses (~256 tokens) we'd like p95 under 800-1,000 ms. concurrency target is 50-100 concurrent requests sustained during peak windows, spikes to 200 for a few minutes. streaming is important - we stream partial responses to clients as tokens arrive.
[01:08] Lara Gomez: and for some high-value flows we need end-to-end p95 tighter, so low jitter matters more than absolute median.
[01:15] Ravi Patel: good context. so rough mapping: hosted can generally hit your med latencies but multi-tenant variance can add jitter on p95 for sustained high concurrency. Dedicated gives predictable throughput - you reserve GPU pools with deterministic latency. Private (VPC/on-prem) removes network hop variability but adds ops overhead.
[01:32] Ethan Wu: what's the typical p95 you see for 32-token completion on dedicated? any numbers?
[01:36] Ravi Patel: on our Dedicated 80/100-config with A100-type nodes and optimized kernel paths, we've seen p95 ~120-220 ms for 32-token responses when batching is minimal and kv/prefix cache warm. But that depends on model size and quantization. For 256-token outputs p95 tends to be 600-950 ms in our benchmarks at concurrency 20-50.
[02:00] Ethan Wu: ok that's promising. how about streaming and token/sec throughput? our product requires ~300 tokens/sec sustained per node at peak across many sessions.
[02:10] Ravi Patel: tokens/sec is pretty model dependent. for a 7B to 13B family with quantized int8 and optimized attention kernels, you can hit ~1k-3k tokens/sec per GPU under ideal conditions. But with streaming and many concurrent sessions we focus on latency per request rather than raw aggregate tokens/sec. For throughput at concurrency 100, we use sharded pools and continuous batching; effective tokens/sec scales but you trade a bit of tail latency.
[02:35] Priya Desai: from security side - can dedicated run inside our VPC? we need KMS for key management and SAML SSO integration.
[02:44] Maya Chen: yes - Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and Private deployment offers customer-managed control plane. We integrate with KMS/HSM and SAML SSO; we'll share SOC2/ISO docs.
[02:55] Lara Gomez: what's the cold start profile and warmup behavior? we can't tolerate big p95 spikes on first request.
[03:02] Ravi Patel: cold starts are primarily model load time and cache population. For Dedicated we keep models resident; for Hosted we keep hot models on warm nodes but there may be occasional evictions. We mitigate with prefix/KV caching and pre-warming. Cold loads for large models can be several seconds; for production critical flows we recommend Dedicated or Private so you avoid those spikes.
[03:22] Ethan Wu: can you run benchmarks with our actual prompt set? we need apples-to-apples numbers for 32/128/512 token outputs with streaming enabled and concurrency 20/50/100.
[03:31] Ravi Patel: yes we can. recommended approach: you share canonical prompts, we'll provision a short-lived Dedicated cluster or hosted test with pinned capacity, run token/sec and p95 measurements across target concurrencies and token lengths, and return a report. that'll show median and p95, plus distribution and CPU/GPU utilization.
[03:48] Noah Kim: what about network topology - if we peer via VPC, how does latency look? any recommended region placement?
[03:54] Maya Chen: we recommend colocating with your app region to minimize RTT; VPC peering and private endpoints reduce network hops. We'll work with your infra on region selection; for strict p95 you may want a dedicated cluster in the region nearest your users.
[04:08] Priya Desai: do you have audit logs and per-token billing traces? we need to show data flows for compliance.
[04:13] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. You can also restrict retention and export logs for audits.
[04:22] Ethan Wu: curious about fallbacks - if a dedicated pool is saturated do you route to hosted or lower-quality model? how does that impact user experience?
[04:30] Ravi Patel: good question. we have smart routing and fallbacks: policies can route to cheaper quantized variants or hosted fallback with slightly higher latency. For critical flows you can set hard limits to reject or queue; for non-critical we recommend graded fallback (smaller model or degraded output). We'll show options in the runbook.
[04:48] Lara Gomez: pricing - rough idea of cost difference dedicated vs hosted?
[04:52] Maya Chen: high level: Hosted is usage-based (per token) and good for variable loads; Dedicated is reserved capacity with lower unit cost and predictable throughput. We'll send a short comparison with sample math based on your peak concurrency.
[05:02] Ethan Wu: on benchmarks - please measure p95 across windows (1m, 5m) and report jitter and tail. Also include streaming latency (time-to-first-byte) and time-per-token.
[05:12] Ravi Patel: absolutely. we'll include time-to-first-token and per-token latency after initial token. For streaming we instrument both TTFB and token spacing.
[05:19] Priya Desai: can you share SOC2 report and details of KMS integration?
[05:23] Maya Chen: yes i'll attach SOC2 docs and our security whitepaper. we'll also include network architecture for Private deployment.
[05:30] Lara Gomez: ok recap and next steps?
[05:33] Maya Chen: recap: we will run a benchmark with your prompt set covering 32/128/512 outputs at concurrencies 20/50/100, measure median/p95/time-to-first-token and tokens/sec, and compare Hosted vs Dedicated. maya -> send pricing and security docs by fri 5/1. ravi -> benchmark plan + provisioning by mon 5/4. sierra -> upload prompts and target p95s by fri 5/1. schedule tech deep dive week of 5/4.
[05:56] Ethan Wu: sounds good. any blockers on our side?
[05:58] Priya Desai: nothing else, just want the security docs before we sign any test infra access.
[06:03] Maya Chen: understood - we'll send docs first, then provision test infra. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite.
[06:10] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript has some auto-speech errors; proper nouns sometimes mis-recognized. Model performance numbers are approximations and depend on exact model, quantization, seq length.
